firstPlayerRule: The player who is best at keeping their word starts.
clarifications: That player takes the Start Player marker; turns proceed clockwise. The marker passes to the player on the left in later rounds.
internalEvidence: Rendered PDF page 2 gives the keeping-one’s-word criterion and clockwise direction; page 4 explains marker handoff. Funding board, 72 Fund cards and Time wheels match inventory BGG 180899. Original publisher identity cross-checked against the BGG game record; the archived booklet itself has no publisher imprint. SHA-256: a0ab4082502fb17b3f4fb5276c001b38d2be86dbffbaadc8754590b3a955ab3d. Owner authorized assistant review on 2026-09-22. Editorial review 2026-09-24: Rechecked the opening instruction, game identity and named edition against the rendered rulebook.
uncertainty: The subjective criterion has no objective test or tie procedure.

fairUse.rationale: Small plain product box image identifies the precise original edition discussed in this starting-rule article. It is used for editorial reference with no more package artwork than needed for identification.
fairUse.provenance: Noble Knight listing https://www.nobleknight.com/P/2148005862/Ponzi-Scheme-Multilingual-Edition explicitly identifies Homosapiens Lab, Jesse Li, the 2015 multilingual boxed game, and hosts this isolated box front. Jesse Li's original creator campaign https://www.flyingv.cc/projects/4303?lang=en confirms the 2015 original project; the publisher-authored multilingual rules depict the matching original components. A contemporary 2015 review https://opinionatedgamers.com/2015/08/19/dale-yu-first-impressions-of-ponzi-scheme/ shows the same finished handshake box and identifies its publisher and multilingual rules, distinguishing it from later TMG and Bright Eye editions. The image itself is retailer-hosted, and no permission is implied.
